messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE FIRED: autoscaler.capacity-exhaustion on service=inference-queue env=prod (triggered by queue_backlog > 10000)

pagerduty: Incident 24f3b - Capacity exhaustion (inference-queue) - Paging alice

alice: acked via PD. I'm on it.

alice: seeing huge queue length across shards, latency spiking to 2.3s for generation requests. Some 502s coming from router.

ben: adding context — autoscaler HPA isn't increasing replicas. `kubectl get hpa inference-workers -n prod` shows current=3 desired=3 even though metrics show CPU low but queue length high.

alice: exact logs from autoscaler:
```
I0310 12:34:21.123] HorizontalPodAutoscaler: no metrics available for inference-workers, skip scaling
I0310 12:34:21.124] error: metrics API returned: unauthorized when accessing custom metrics
```

carla: so metrics-server or RBAC to metrics API? we hit this before with upgraded cluster auth.

nate: @alice can you run a quick `kubectl auth can-i get --raw "/apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1" -n prod` and `kubectl get --raw /apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1`?

alice: running...
```
$ kubectl auth can-i get --raw "/apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1" -n prod
no
```

alice: ok that explains it. HPA can't read queue-length metric. recent kube upgrade probably tightened auth for the metrics adapter serviceaccount.

ben: can we patch temporarily by giving the autoscaler SA clusterrole to read custom metrics? quick and dirty to buy time.

carla: prefer to patch the metrics-adapter role to include `custom.metrics.k8s.io` get/list. but if we need immediate capacity, manual scale of deployment is fastest.

alice: manual scaling attempt to reduce user impact. increasing replicas from 3 -> 12:
```
kubectl scale deployment inference-workers -n prod --replicas=12
```

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: action logged: manual scale to 12 replicas by alice

devops-bot: note: cluster has quotas on GPU node groups; autoscaler was expected to spin up nodes but node-group autoscaler shows scale up blocked: `nodegroup/gpu-prod` is at max size 10.

nate: then also need burst capacity config in routing to avoid overloading worker pool. can we enable temporary cpu-only workers for low-accuracy fallback?

ben: there's a config toggle in infra-config map: `enable_burst_cpu_workers: false`. flipping may help soak backlog without waiting for GPUs. I can patch it.

alice: do it. patch below and restart router to pick up config.
```
kubectl -n prod patch configmap infra-config --patch '{"data":{"enable_burst_cpu_workers":"true"}}'
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/router
```

ben: patched and restarted router. Router logs show fallback pool spinning up.

alice: we're seeing queue drain rate increase, backlog dropping from 11.2k -> 6.8k in 3m. p95 latency down to 900ms. still some customer timeouts earlier.

carla: good progress. we still need to fix the metrics RBAC to restore autoscaler. who's on infra to push an RBAC fix?

nate: I'll prepare the rolebinding change and drop it to canary, then apply prod. posting the RBAC snippet: 
```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: metrics-reader-extra
rules:
- apiGroups: ["custom.metrics.k8s.io"]
  resources: ["*"]
  verbs: ["get","list","watch"]
```

ben: ensure serviceaccount for `metrics-adapter` is bound to that clusterrole. Once HPA can read metrics, it should scale back down/up as needed.

alice: status update for ops-channel in 5: I'll include impact assessment: ~10% customer requests saw >1.5s latency, small percent 502s. No data loss, just degraded latency.

sre_lead: can you add list of affected customers (by org-id) to the incident doc? Ops will decide if we need a customer-facing message.

alice: adding to incident page: https://redwood.prod/incidents/24f3b (private) — note: org-42, org-108, org-204 had the highest error rate.

alice: applying RBAC patch to prod now (will wait 30s for review).

ben: quick sanity check — after RBAC change we should see HPA desired go > current if queue metric present. watch HPA and metrics API.

nate: RBAC applied. metrics-adapter logs show successful read on custom metric `queue_length` now.

alice: query HPA: desired=20 current=12 -> autoscaler trying to scale. but node-group limit still blocks further nodes. we need to request temporary node-group increase or move some pods to CPU fallback pool.

carla: I'll open a temporary nodegroup increase with infra-oncall (ticket INF-9876). also we can cordon some noncritical GPU pods to free GPUs.

devops-bot: INFRA: ticket INF-9876 created to increase nodegroup/gpu-prod max size by 5.

alice: after manual scaling + burst CPU workers + RBAC fix, queue is now 1200 and trending down. p95 back to 380ms.

ben: recommend we keep burst CPU workers enabled for 30m and then revert once backlog cleared to avoid cost. Also follow-up: reconcile cluster upgrade RBAC change permanently.

carla: I'll take handoff in 25m. alice do you want to write the postmortem starter and assign owners for RBAC change, nodegroup sizing, and autoscaler monitoring?

alice: will do. quick public blurb for status page: "We experienced increased request latency and queue backlog due to metrics RBAC regression that prevented autoscaling. Temporary mitigations (manual scale, CPU fallback) reduced customer impact. Full fix in progress."

nate: marking incident as active -> mitigated in PD once backlog under 2k and p95 < 500ms.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: page acknowledged by alice; status: mitigated, follow-ups created.

carla: taking over. if anything spikes ping me @carla. I'll monitor until next rotation.

alice: thanks team. I'll draft follow-ups and the postmortem draft in the incident doc.

ben: good work. lesson: validate RBAC after cluster upgrades in canary clusters.

carla: handoff complete. closing thread in 1h after validation.
